overview.title: Welcome to Dakhla — lagoon, wind and the edge of the desert
overview.p1: Dakhla sits on a long peninsula in southern Morocco, between a vast turquoise lagoon and the open Atlantic. Trade winds, flat water and empty shores have made it one of Africa’s leading spots for kitesurf and wingfoil — but the place is more than a sports camp.
overview.p2: Beyond the water: the White Dune rising from the lagoon, Dragon Island’s rocky silhouette, oyster farms on the water, Foum El Bouir on the ocean side, and desert tracks toward Sebkha Imlili. Town life is calm; most days revolve around wind, light and the horizon.
overview.p3: Three to seven days work well if you mix water time with dune outings and slower lagoon evenings.

itinerary.title: Suggested 4-day plan for Dakhla
itinerary.subtitle: Wind and lagoon first, then dunes and ocean side.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Transfer from Dakhla Airport; check in near the lagoon or in town.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Walk the shore, note wind direction, plan tomorrow’s session.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Quiet light over the lagoon; simple dinner.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Kitesurf or wingfoil on the lagoon’s calm water.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: More water time or relaxing at a shore-side café.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: An evening by the lagoon or along the waterfront.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Drive or take a boat toward the White Dune to enjoy the views.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Spot the rocky formation, take photos, and enjoy the lagoon light.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Taste lagoon oysters if in season.
detailed_itinerary.day4_m: Morning — Foum El Bouir or Sebkha Imlili
detailed_itinerary.day4_md: Ocean waves on the far side or a track on the edge of the desert.
detailed_itinerary.day4_a: Afternoon — Free Time or Second Session

detailed_itinerary.day4_ed: Final sunset if flight schedules allow.

q1.question: How many days in Dakhla?
q1.answer: 3 to 4 days cover lagoon orientation, sports sessions, White Dune and Foum El Bouir. 5 to 7 days suit dedicated kitesurfers.

q2.question: Is Dakhla only for kitesurf?
q2.answer: Wind sports are the main draw, but the lagoon, White Dune, Dragon Island, oysters and desert edge work for non-riders too.

q3.question: How do I get to Dakhla?
q3.answer: Fly into Dakhla Airport (VIL). Domestic flights link from Casablanca and other cities; overland is a long southern road journey.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: Wind is present much of the year. October to June is popular for comfortable temperatures and reliable sessions.
